claim: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis is an essential process that forms vesicles from the plasma membrane.
source: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis is an essential process that forms vesicles from the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in cell biology, representing established scientific consensus.

claim: The organization of endocytic proteins at the endocytic site is poorly understood.
source: Although most of the protein components of the endocytic protein machinery have been thoroughly characterized, their organization at the endocytic site is poorly understood.
evidence: This statement characterizes the state of knowledge in the field prior to the study.

claim: The authors developed a fluorescence microscopy method to track the average positions of yeast endocytic proteins with a time precision below 1 s and spatial precision of ~10 nm.
source: We developed a fluorescence microscopy method to track the average positions of yeast endocytic proteins in relation to each other with a time precision below 1 s and with a spatial precision of ∼10 nm.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the method developed and its precision, supported by the experimental data and validation presented in the manuscript.

claim: Different coat proteins are distributed within the coat structure in specific patterns.
source: We showed how different coat proteins are distributed within the coat structure and how the assembly dynamics of N-BAR proteins relate to membrane shape changes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the tracking data and analysis presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The region of actin polymerization is located at the base of the endocytic invagination, with the growing ends of filaments pointing toward the plasma membrane.
source: Moreover, we found that the region of actin polymerization is located at the base of the endocytic invagination, with the growing ends of filaments pointing toward the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is supported by the photobleaching experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis is involved in numerous different biological contexts from the generation of cellular polarization, to virus uptake and the regulation of neural signaling.
source: It is involved in numerous different biological contexts from the generation of cellular polarization, to virus uptake and the regulation of neural signaling.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about the biological roles of clathrin-mediated endocytosis.

claim: The formation of clathrin-coated endocytic vesicles is driven by a complex molecular machinery composed of more than 50 different proteins.
source: The formation of clathrin-coated endocytic vesicles is driven by a complex molecular machinery composed of more than 50 different proteins (Doherty and McMahon, 2009; Boettner et al., 2012; Weinberg and Drubin, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The assembly dynamics of the endocytic protein machinery has been described in detail by live-cell imaging.
source: The assembly dynamics of the endocytic protein machinery has been described in detail by live-cell imaging (Gaidarov et al., 1999; Merrifield et al., 2002; Kaksonen et al., 2003, 2005; Newpher et al., 2005; Sirotkin et al., 2010; Loerke et al., 2011; Taylor et al., 2011; Cocucci et al., 2012; Berro and Pollard, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The spatial organization of the endocytic proteins during vesicle budding remains poorly understood.
source: However, the spatial organization of the endocytic proteins during vesicle budding remains poorly understood.
evidence: This characterizes the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The complexity and the size of the endocytic machinery, below the resolution limit of light microscopy, have made it challenging to reveal how the endocytic proteins are organized during vesicle budding.
source: The complexity and the size of the endocytic machinery, below the resolution limit of light microscopy, have made it challenging to reveal how the endocytic proteins are organized during vesicle budding.
evidence: This explains the technical challenge that motivated the development of the new method.

claim: Budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae has been used extensively as a model organism to study endocytosis.
source: Budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae has been used extensively as a model organism to study endocytosis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the use of yeast as a model system.

claim: The protein machinery of clathrin-mediated endocytosis is largely conserved between mammals and yeast.
source: The protein machinery of clathrin-mediated endocytosis is largely conserved between mammals and yeast (Conibear, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In yeast, endocytosis starts with the recruitment of clathrin and several clathrin adaptors and accessory proteins to the plasma membrane to initiate the assembly of the vesicle coat.
source: In yeast, endocytosis starts with the recruitment of clathrin and several clathrin adaptors and accessory proteins to the plasma membrane to initiate the assembly of the vesicle coat (Carroll et al., 2012; Godlee and Kaksonen, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: During the initial early phase of endocytosis, which can last between 40 and 90 s, the coat assembles on a flat plasma membrane and cargo molecules are recruited to the endocytic site.
source: During this initial early phase, which can last between 40 and 90 s, the coat assembles on a flat plasma membrane and cargo molecules are recruited to the endocytic site.
evidence: This describes the temporal and functional characteristics of the early phase of endocytosis based on established knowledge.

claim: Las17 is the yeast homolog of mammalian N-WASP.
source: The actin interactors include Las17 (homolog of mammalian N-WASP) and type I myosins Myo3 and Myo5, which both activate the actin filament nucleating Arp2/3 complex (Winter et al., 1999; Evangelista et al., 2000; Lechler et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Type I myosins Myo3 and Myo5 activate the actin filament nucleating Arp2/3 complex.
source: The actin interactors include Las17 (homolog of mammalian N-WASP) and type I myosins Myo3 and Myo5, which both activate the actin filament nucleating Arp2/3 complex (Winter et al., 1999; Evangelista et al., 2000; Lechler et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In yeast, the invagination of the plasma membrane and the consequent inward movement of the coat is concomitant with the appearance of actin at the endocytic site.
source: In yeast, the invagination of the plasma membrane, and the consequent inward movement of the coat, is concomitant with the appearance of actin at the endocytic site (Kukulski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A functional dependence on actin polymerization in yeast is possibly due to high turgor pressure.
source: A functional dependence on actin polymerization is possibly due to high turgor pressure (Aghamohammadzadeh and Ayscough, 2009).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation.

claim: In mammals, actin is similarly critical under conditions of high membrane tension.
source: In mammals, actin is similarly critical under conditions of high membrane tension (Boulant et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Sla2 is the homolog of mammalian Hip1R.
source: Two of the coat-associated proteins, Sla2 (homolog of mammalian Hip1R) and the epsin Ent1, interact directly with lipids, clathrin and actin, and are essential for mediating the forces from the actin cytoskeleton to deform the membrane (Baggett et al., 2003; Sun et al., 2005; Skruzny et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sla2 and the epsin Ent1 interact directly with lipids, clathrin and actin, and are essential for mediating the forces from the actin cytoskeleton to deform the membrane.
source: Two of the coat-associated proteins, Sla2 (homolog of mammalian Hip1R) and the epsin Ent1, interact directly with lipids, clathrin and actin, and are essential for mediating the forces from the actin cytoskeleton to deform the membrane (Baggett et al., 2003; Sun et al., 2005; Skruzny et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The Rvs161/167 heterodimer is localized at the neck region of the membrane invagination.
source: The shape of the endocytic invagination is regulated by proteins containing BAR domains, such as the Rvs161/167 heterodimer, which are localized at the neck region of the membrane invagination (Idrissi et al., 2008; Youn et al., 2010; Kishimoto et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: After vesicle scission the endocytic machinery quickly disassembles and the free vesicle is trafficked further into the cell.
source: After vesicle scission the endocytic machinery quickly disassembles and the free vesicle is trafficked further into the cell.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about the final stages of endocytosis.

claim: The exact molecular mechanisms of endocytosis remain unknown, largely due to lack of knowledge about the functional organization of the protein components of the endocytic machinery.
source: The exact molecular mechanisms of endocytosis remain unknown, largely due to lack of knowledge about the functional organization of the protein components of the endocytic machinery.
evidence: This characterizes the gap in knowledge that motivates the study.

claim: The authors used wide-field epifluorescence microscopy to image GFP-tagged endocytic proteins expressed from their endogenous genomic loci in haploid cells of yeast S cerevisiae.
source: We used wide-field epifluorescence microscopy to image GFP-tagged endocytic proteins expressed from their endogenous genomic loci in haploid cells of yeast S cerevisiae.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Videos were acquired at the equatorial plane of the yeast cells, where the average direction of endocytic vesicle budding is planar with the focal plane.
source: We acquired videos at the equatorial plane of the yeast cells, where the average direction of endocytic vesicle budding is planar with the focal plane (Kaksonen et al., 2003; Kukulski et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the imaging approach and is supported by citations.

claim: In yeast, the dynamic behavior of the endocytic proteins during vesicle budding is highly stereotypical.
source: In yeast, the dynamic behavior of the endocytic proteins during vesicle budding is highly stereotypical (Kaksonen et al., 2003; Mooren et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The centroid gives an estimate of the position of the center of mass of the protein distribution.
source: The centroid gives an estimate of the position of the center of mass of the protein distribution; therefore the average trajectory describes the stereotypic dynamic behavior of the center of mass of the target protein molecules during endocytosis.
evidence: This is an inference about what the centroid measurement represents.

claim: The average trajectory describes the stereotypic dynamic behavior of the center of mass of the target protein molecules during endocytosis.
source: The centroid gives an estimate of the position of the center of mass of the protein distribution; therefore the average trajectory describes the stereotypic dynamic behavior of the center of mass of the target protein molecules during endocytosis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the centroid measurement and the stereotypical behavior of endocytic proteins.

claim: The authors estimated the average number of molecules present at the endocytic site by calibrating the fluorescence signal using a kinetochore protein of known abundance.
source: We estimated the average number of molecules present at the endocytic site by calibrating the fluorescence signal using a kinetochore protein of known abundance (Joglekar et al., 2006; Lawrimore et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the method for quantifying protein abundance, supported by citations.

claim: Abp1 was chosen as a reference protein because of its abundance at the endocytic site, which leads to a strong fluorescence signal, and its highly regular dynamic behavior.
source: We chose Abp1 as a reference protein because of its abundance at the endocytic site, which leads to a strong fluorescence signal, and its highly regular dynamic behavior, which is directed perpendicular to the cell surface thereby defining the direction of the invagination movement (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This explains the rationale for choosing Abp1 as a reference, supported by data in supplementary figures.

claim: Abp1's dynamic behavior is directed perpendicular to the cell surface thereby defining the direction of the invagination movement.
source: We chose Abp1 as a reference protein because of its abundance at the endocytic site, which leads to a strong fluorescence signal, and its highly regular dynamic behavior, which is directed perpendicular to the cell surface thereby defining the direction of the invagination movement (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: The standard deviations in space and time of the repeated alignments were 2.8 nm and 0.1 s for Abp1, 5.5 nm and 0.3 s for Rvs167 and 12.9 nm and 0.6 s for Sla2.
source: The standard deviations in space and time of the repeated alignments were 2.8 nm and 0.1 s for Abp1, 5.5 nm and 0.3 s for Rvs167 and 12.9 nm and 0.6 s for Sla2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The accuracies of the alignments correlate with the signal intensities of these different proteins.
source: The accuracies of the alignments correlate with the signal intensities of these different proteins.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed relationship between signal intensity and alignment accuracy.

claim: With experimentally relevant noise levels the trajectories aligned within 3 nm from the ground truth trajectory.
source: With experimentally relevant noise levels the trajectories aligned within 3 nm from the ground truth trajectory (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: With realistic color shifts (up to 50 nm) the average trajectories are only about 3 nm from the ground truth trajectory.
source: With realistic color shifts (up to 50 nm) the average trajectories are only about 3 nm from the ground truth trajectory (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: With the average trajectories the authors can resolve the position and movement of different endocytic components in relation to each other along the direction of invagination with a temporal precision below 1 s and with a spatial precision of ~10 nm.
source: In summary, with the average trajectories we can resolve the position and movement of different endocytic components in relation to each other along the direction of invagination with a temporal precision below 1 s and with a spatial precision of ∼10 nm.
evidence: This summarizes the precision of the method based on the validation experiments.

claim: The authors aligned the trajectories with time-resolved average membrane shapes obtained previously by CLEM.
source: To provide a framework for interpreting the tracking data, we aligned the trajectories with time-resolved average membrane shapes obtained previously by CLEM (Kukulski et al., 2012), starting from a flat membrane and ending with a vesicle (Figure 2).
evidence: This describes the integration of the tracking data with previous EM data, shown in Figure 2.

claim: The authors used Sla2, Rvs167 and Abp1 proteins as spatial and temporal landmarks to align the membrane shapes from the CLEM study to their tracking data.
source: We used Sla2, Rvs167 and Abp1 proteins as spatial and temporal landmarks to align the membrane shapes from the CLEM study to our tracking data.
evidence: This describes the approach for aligning the tracking data with membrane shapes.

claim: The binding of Sla2's ANTH domain to PIP2 at the plasma membrane is essential for productive endocytosis.
source: The binding of Sla2's ANTH domain to PIP2 at the plasma membrane is essential for productive endocytosis (Sun et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Before membrane bending starts, the centroid of GFP-Sla2 is likely to be within few nm from the plasma membrane surface.
source: We could therefore assume that before membrane bending starts (first time point in Figure 2A,C) the centroid of GFP-Sla2 is likely to be within few nm from the plasma membrane surface, whose position we took as the origin of the position axis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known binding of Sla2's ANTH domain to the membrane.

claim: Sla2 molecules cover a ~30–40 nm long region at the tip of the invagination.
source: We then calculated the positions of the center of mass of Sla2 molecules on the shapes of the different membrane intermediates taking into account that Sla2 molecules cover a ∼30–40 nm long region at the tip of the invagination (Idrissi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The start of Abp1 assembly coincides with initial membrane bending.
source: Our alignment agreed well with the time resolved data from CLEM study: the start of Abp1 assembly coincides with initial membrane bending, and the assembly of Rvs167 starts when the invaginations are ∼50 nm long (Kukulski et al., 2012) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with previous CLEM data and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The assembly of Rvs167 starts when the invaginations are ~50 nm long.
source: Our alignment agreed well with the time resolved data from CLEM study: the start of Abp1 assembly coincides with initial membrane bending, and the assembly of Rvs167 starts when the invaginations are ∼50 nm long (Kukulski et al., 2012) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with previous CLEM data and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The CLEM data indicated that on average the vesicle scission takes place when ~59% of the Rvs167-GFP patch lifetime has passed.
source: The CLEM data also indicated that on average the vesicle scission takes place when ∼59% of the Rvs167-GFP patch lifetime has passed (Kukulski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous CLEM data.

claim: The time at which the number of Rvs167-GFP molecules peaks coincides with the scission time.
source: This time point coincides with the peak number of Rvs167-GFP molecules (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Sla2 is critical for membrane-actin coupling during vesicle budding.
source: Sla2 is critical for membrane-actin coupling during vesicle budding (Sun et al., 2005; Boettner et al., 2011; Skruzny et al., 2012), whereas Sla1 and End3 are involved in the regulation of the initiation of actin polymerization (Tang et al., 2000; Rodal et al., 2003; Kaksonen et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sla1 and End3 are involved in the regulation of the initiation of actin polymerization.
source: Sla2 is critical for membrane-actin coupling during vesicle budding (Sun et al., 2005; Boettner et al., 2011; Skruzny et al., 2012), whereas Sla1 and End3 are involved in the regulation of the initiation of actin polymerization (Tang et al., 2000; Rodal et al., 2003; Kaksonen et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sla2 is composed of the N-terminal lipid-binding ANTH domain and a C-terminal actin-binding domain, which are separated by a long coiled-coil region.
source: Sla2 is composed of the N-terminal lipid-binding ANTH domain and a C-terminal actin-binding domain, which are separated by a long coiled-coil region.
evidence: This describes the known structure of Sla2.

claim: In Hip1R, the mammalian homolog of Sla2, the coiled-coil region has been measured to be ~40 nm long.
source: In Hip1R, the mammalian homolog of Sla2, the coiled-coil region has been measured to be ∼40 nm long (Engqvist-Goldstein et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Both GFP-Sla2 and Sla2-GFP average trajectories exhibited an initial motionless phase followed by inward movement.
source: Both GFP-Sla2 and Sla2-GFP average trajectories exhibited an initial motionless phase followed by inward movement.
evidence: This is supported by the tracking data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The Sla2-GFP trajectory was 29 ± 5 nm (mean ± SE) distant from the GFP-Sla2 trajectory during the initial non-motile phase.
source: However, the Sla2-GFP trajectory was 29 ± 5 nm (mean ± SE) distant from the GFP-Sla2 trajectory during the initial non-motile phase (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: GFP-Sla2-mCherry molecules were oriented perpendicularly to the plasma membrane.
source: The GFP-Sla2-mCherry molecules were oriented perpendicularly to the plasma membrane (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and the distance between the centroids of the GFP and mCherry tags was 33 ± 3.4 nm (mean ± SE) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–F, 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The distance between the centroids of the GFP and mCherry tags in GFP-Sla2-mCherry was 33 ± 3.4 nm (mean ± SE).
source: The GFP-Sla2-mCherry molecules were oriented perpendicularly to the plasma membrane (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and the distance between the centroids of the GFP and mCherry tags was 33 ± 3.4 nm (mean ± SE) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–F, 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: The distance between the centroids of the GFP and mCherry tags in GFP-Sla2-mCherry compares well with the average distance between GFP-Sla2 and Sla2-GFP average trajectories during the initial motionless phase.
source: This compares well with the average distance between GFP-Sla2 and Sla2-GFP average trajectories during the initial motionless phase.
evidence: This is an inference comparing two independent measurements.

claim: Sla2 molecules are oriented within the coat so that the PIP2 binding N-terminal domain is at the membrane and the actin-binding C-terminal domain projects into the cytoplasm.
source: These results indicate that Sla2 molecules are oriented within the coat so that the PIP2 binding N-terminal domain is at the membrane and the actin-binding C-terminal domain projects into the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is an inference based on the tracking data and the double-labeling experiments.

claim: When the membrane invagination starts, the GFP-Sla2 and Sla2-GFP centroids start moving inward and the distance between them becomes shorter.
source: When the membrane invagination starts, the GFP-Sla2 and Sla2-GFP centroids start moving inward and the distance between them becomes shorter (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: During invagination the Sla2 molecules would reorient to accommodate membrane bending and the center of mass positions of their N and C-termini would move closer to each other.
source: A simple explanation for this convergence is that the Sla2 molecules maintain a constant orientation with respect to the membrane. Therefore, during invagination the Sla2 molecules would reorient to accommodate membrane bending and the center of mass positions of their N and C-termini would move closer to each other (Figure 3A, right panel, time points −7, −6 and −4 s).
evidence: This is a proposed explanation for the observed convergence of trajectories.

claim: A conformational change of Sla2 could also contribute to the convergence of the trajectories by bringing the N- and C-termini closer to each other.
source: Alternatively, a conformational change of Sla2 could also contribute to the convergence of the trajectories by bringing the N- and C-termini closer to each other.
evidence: This is an alternative speculative explanation for the observed convergence.

claim: The average trajectories of Sla1-GFP and End3-GFP had very similar shapes, but were separated by about ~10 nm or more.
source: The average trajectories of Sla1-GFP and End3-GFP had very similar shapes, but were separated by about ∼10 nm or more (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The number of Sla2 molecules remained relatively constant at ~40 molecules during vesicle budding and started to drop ~2–3 s before scission.
source: The number of Sla2 molecules remained relatively constant at ∼40 molecules during vesicle budding and started to drop ∼2–3 s before scission (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Sla1 and End3 molecules peaked at ~90 and ~60 molecules respectively and started disassembling already during invagination.
source: Sla1 and End3 molecules peaked at ∼90 and ∼60 molecules respectively and started disassembling already during invagination (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The Sla2 centroid started moving ~2 s before the Sla1 and End3 centroids and moved past the Sla1 centroid during invagination.
source: However, the Sla2 centroid started moving ∼2 s before the Sla1 and End3 centroids and moved past the Sla1 centroid during invagination (Figure 3B, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Sla2, Sla1 and End3 are not distributed similarly within the coat.
source: This suggests that Sla2, Sla1 and End3 are not distributed similarly within the coat.
evidence: This is an inference based on the different trajectories of these proteins.

claim: Sla2 is located on the invagination tip and Sla1 and End3 are located at the rim of the coat.
source: The observed trajectories could result from Sla2 being located on the invagination tip and Sla1 and End3 being located at the rim of the coat (Figure 3B, right panel).
evidence: This is a proposed model to explain the observed trajectories, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: When the membrane starts bending, Sla2 molecules would start moving first, followed slightly later by Sla1 and End3 molecules.
source: With such distributions, when the membrane starts bending, Sla2 molecules would start moving first, followed slightly later by Sla1 and End3 molecules.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the proposed model of protein distribution.

claim: Sla1 was localized in ring shapes.
source: With an average localization precision of approximately 10 nm, we could directly observe that Sla1 was localized in ring shapes (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B,E).
evidence: This is supported by superresolution microscopy data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Latrunculin A inhibits actin polymerization and prevents membrane bending.
source: To exclude the possibility that a ring was observed because we were imaging a curved membrane, we treated Sla1-SNAP expressing cells with Latrunculin A, which inhibits actin polymerization and prevents membrane bending (Kukulski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Ring-shaped Sla1 structures were observed even when the plasma membrane remained flat after Latrunculin A treatment.
source: Again, we observed ring-shaped Sla1 structures (Figure 3E) even though the plasma membrane remained flat (Figure 3—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2H.

claim: Sla1 is organized in a circular pattern at the endocytic site prior to membrane invagination.
source: These results show that Sla1 is organized in a circular pattern at the endocytic site prior to membrane invagination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the superresolution imaging data.

claim: The BAR domain proteins Rvs161 and Rvs167 form stable heterodimers.
source: The BAR domain proteins Rvs161 and Rvs167 form stable heterodimers, which localize transiently to the neck region of the endocytic invagination where they are thought to regulate vesicle scission (Kaksonen et al., 2005; Ren et al., 2006; Idrissi et al., 2008; Youn et al., 2010; Kishimoto et al., 2011; Kukulski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rvs161/167 heterodimers localize transiently to the neck region of the endocytic invagination where they are thought to regulate vesicle scission.
source: The BAR domain proteins Rvs161 and Rvs167 form stable heterodimers, which localize transiently to the neck region of the endocytic invagination where they are thought to regulate vesicle scission (Kaksonen et al., 2005; Ren et al., 2006; Idrissi et al., 2008; Youn et al., 2010; Kishimoto et al., 2011; Kukulski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The average trajectory of Rvs167-GFP showed three different phases.
source: The average trajectory of Rvs167-GFP showed three different phases (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: During the first phase of Rvs167-GFP dynamics, the centroid moved inward linearly less than 15 nm while the Rvs167-GFP molecules assembled at a constant rate of ~40 molecules/s.
source: During the first phase the centroid moved inward linearly less than 15 nm while the Rvs167-GFP molecules assembled at a constant rate of ∼40 molecules/s (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: In the next phase of Rvs167-GFP dynamics, the centroid moved rapidly for ~100 nm in less than a second.
source: In the next phase the centroid moved rapidly for ∼100 nm (Figure 4A) in less than a second.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The rapid centroid movement of Rvs167-GFP coincided with a transition to disassembly and with the scission of the vesicle.
source: This rapid centroid movement coincided with a transition to disassembly and with the scission of the vesicle (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In the last phase of Rvs167-GFP dynamics, the centroid continues to move inward, but with a reduced rate.
source: In the last phase the centroid continues to move inward, but with a reduced rate (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The fast centroid movement of the Rvs proteins has been described before, but its mechanism remained unknown.
source: The fast centroid movement of the Rvs proteins has been described before, but its mechanism remained unknown (Kaksonen et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BAR domains can form regular oligomeric structures on membrane tubules of varying diameters.
source: These studies have shown that BAR domains can form regular oligomeric structures on membrane tubules of varying diameters, giving us an estimate of the density of dimers on the membrane.
evidence: This is based on citations to structural studies of BAR domain proteins.

claim: Rvs proteins start assembling at the midpoint of the endocytic invagination and the Rvs covered membrane area increases linearly and reaches its maximum at about the time of scission.
source: This reconstruction of Rvs localization revealed the dynamics of Rvs assembly and disassembly in relation to membrane invagination and scission (Figure 4C). Rvs proteins start assembling at the midpoint of the endocytic invagination and the Rvs covered membrane area increases linearly and reaches its maximum at about the time of scission.
evidence: This is supported by the reconstruction model shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Immediately prior to scission there are enough Rvs molecules to cover the whole tubular part of the invagination from the base of the invagination to the coated tip.
source: Immediately prior to scission there are enough Rvs molecules to cover the whole tubular part of the invagination from the base of the invagination to the coated tip (Figure 4C; time point 0).
evidence: This is supported by the reconstruction model shown in Figure 4C.

claim: After reaching their peak number, the Rvs molecules disassemble rapidly and their center of mass moves quickly inward toward the region where the newly formed vesicle is located.
source: After reaching their peak number, the Rvs molecules disassemble rapidly (Figure 4B) and their center of mass moves quickly inward toward the region where the newly formed vesicle is located.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The rapid movement of the Rvs centroid is the result of a rapid disassembly of the Rvs molecules at the neck of the invagination, where scission occurs, while some of the Rvs molecules are kept at the vesicle surface where they stay ~2 s longer.
source: Our reconstruction suggests that the rapid movement of the centroid is the result of a rapid disassembly of the Rvs molecules at the neck of the invagination, where scission occurs (Kukulski et al., 2012), while some of the Rvs molecules are kept at the vesicle surface where they stay ∼2 s longer.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reconstruction model and previous CLEM data.

claim: Polymerization of actin filaments at the endocytic site is critical for membrane invagination and vesicle budding.
source: Polymerization of actin filaments at the endocytic site is critical for membrane invagination and vesicle budding (Merrifield et al., 2002; Kaksonen et al., 2003; Boulant et al., 2011; Idrissi et al., 2012; Kukulski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The endocytic actin filaments are nucleated by the Arp2/3 complex, which binds to existing filaments and nucleates new filaments in a branched configuration.
source: The endocytic actin filaments are nucleated by the Arp2/3 complex, which binds to existing filaments and nucleates new filaments in a branched configuration.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about actin nucleation by the Arp2/3 complex.

claim: Actin filaments are organized as a dense, branched network, which surrounds the endocytic site and the newly formed vesicle.

claim: The centroids of Act1, Arc18 and Abp1 moved for ~100 nm until the scission time.

claim: The tight colocalization of the centroids of Act1, Arc18 and Abp1 suggests that they are homogeneously distributed within the actin network.
source: The tight colocalization of the centroids of Act1, Arc18 and Abp1 suggests that they are homogeneously distributed within the actin network.

claim: After scission the centroid trajectories of Act1, Arc18 and Abp1 became noisier.

claim: The increased noise in the trajectories after scission probably reflects the free diffusion of the actin-covered vesicle in the cytoplasm.

claim: At the beginning of the membrane invagination Las17 and Myo5 average trajectories are close to Act1, Arc18 and Abp1.
source: At the beginning of the membrane invagination Las17 and Myo5 average trajectories are close to Act1, Arc18 and Abp1 (Figure 5A).

claim: The Las17 trajectory moved inward, but much less than Abp1, Arc18 and Act1 trajectories.

claim: The amount of Las17 molecules reached a maximum of ~45 molecules.
source: The amount of Las17 molecules reached a maximum of ∼45 molecules.

source: At ∼2 s before scission the amount of Las17 molecules started decreasing while the number of Act1 molecules reached a plateau which was maintained until the scission event (Figure 5B).

claim: The amount of Arc18 and Myo5 molecules peaked at ~2 s before scission.

claim: The amount of Abp1 molecules peaked at the scission time and then rapidly declined.

claim: GFP-Act1 represented 9 ± 1% of the total cellular actin.

claim: The peak number of actin molecules at the endocytic site is ~3000.

evidence: This is an estimate based on the GFP-Act1 quantification and an assumption about recruitment efficiency.

claim: After photobleaching the reappearing centroids of GFP-Act1 were located closer to the plasma membrane than the centroids at the corresponding time point in the unbleached average trajectory.
source: After photobleaching the reappearing centroids were located closer to the plasma membrane than the centroids at the corresponding time point in the unbleached average trajectory (Figure 6C).

claim: Photobleaching of Arc18-GFP showed a similar, although slightly smaller, shift of the centroid position toward the plasma membrane.
source: We next photobleached Arc18-GFP and observed a similar, although slightly smaller, shift of the centroid position toward the plasma membrane (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by photobleaching data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Actin filament nucleation and polymerization take place at the base of the invagination.
source: These results suggest that actin filament nucleation and polymerization take place at the base of the invagination, in agreement with model 2.

claim: The trajectories of the Abp1-GFP centroid with or without photobleaching did not differ significantly.
source: However, the trajectories of the Abp1-GFP centroid with or without photobleaching did not differ significantly (Figure 6E) suggesting that Abp1 molecules are recruited throughout the actin network unlike actin and the Arp2/3 complex.

claim: Abp1 molecules are recruited throughout the actin network unlike actin and the Arp2/3 complex.
source: However, the trajectories of the Abp1-GFP centroid with or without photobleaching did not differ significantly (Figure 6E) suggesting that Abp1 molecules are recruited throughout the actin network unlike actin and the Arp2/3 complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the photobleaching data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: At all time, GFP-Act1 and Arc18-GFP were added at the base of the invagination.
source: At all time, GFP-Act1 and Arc18-GFP were added at the base of the invagination, but the exact localizations of the two proteins differed: Act1 was added on average at 27 ± 18 nm (mean ± SD, n = 19) and Arc18 at 41 ± 15 nm (mean ± SD, n = 17) above the plasma membrane surface (p value = 0.02).
evidence: This is supported by photobleaching experiments at different time points.

claim: Act1 was added on average at 27 ± 18 nm (mean ± SD, n = 19) above the plasma membrane surface.
source: At all time, GFP-Act1 and Arc18-GFP were added at the base of the invagination, but the exact localizations of the two proteins differed: Act1 was added on average at 27 ± 18 nm (mean ± SD, n = 19) and Arc18 at 41 ± 15 nm (mean ± SD, n = 17) above the plasma membrane surface (p value = 0.02).
evidence: This is supported by photobleaching experiments.

claim: Arc18 was added on average at 41 ± 15 nm (mean ± SD, n = 17) above the plasma membrane surface.
source: At all time, GFP-Act1 and Arc18-GFP were added at the base of the invagination, but the exact localizations of the two proteins differed: Act1 was added on average at 27 ± 18 nm (mean ± SD, n = 19) and Arc18 at 41 ± 15 nm (mean ± SD, n = 17) above the plasma membrane surface (p value = 0.02).
evidence: This is supported by photobleaching experiments.

claim: The Arp2/3 activators Las17 and Myo5 are located at the base of the invagination where actin is added.
source: We note that this is also where the Arp2/3 activators Las17 and Myo5 are located, according to the average centroid trajectories (Figure 6F).

claim: Both actin filament nucleation and polymerization take place at the base of the endocytic invagination.
source: These results suggest that both actin filament nucleation and polymerization take place at the base of the endocytic invagination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the photobleaching experiments.

claim: The Arp2/3 complex is assembled slightly higher above the membrane plane compared to actin, which is consistent with the dendritic nucleation model where the actin plus ends are oriented toward the plasma membrane.
source: The Arp2/3 complex is assembled slightly higher above the membrane plane compared to actin, which is consistent with the dendritic nucleation model (Pollard and Borisy, 2003) where the actin plus ends are oriented toward the plasma membrane (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is an inference based on the photobleaching data and is consistent with the dendritic nucleation model.

claim: Abp1 would be distributed uniformly within the actin network.
source: The putative inhibitor of actin nucleation, Abp1, would be distributed uniformly within the network.
evidence: This is an inference based on the photobleaching data.

claim: The overall assembly dynamics and the stoichiometries of the endocytic proteins are highly similar in S. pombe and S. cerevisiae.
source: Comparing the S. pombe and S. cerevisiae data shows that the overall assembly dynamics and the stoichiometries of the endocytic proteins are highly similar in these very distantly related fungal species.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with previous studies on S. pombe.

claim: The numbers of the S. pombe homologs of Las17 and Myo3/5 also peak briefly before the peak of actin molecules.
source: For example, the numbers of the S. pombe homologs of Las17 and Myo3/5 also peak briefly before the peak of actin molecules (Berro et al., 2010; Sirotkin et al., 2010), suggesting that the assembly dynamics of the actin cytoskeleton are functionally optimized.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on S. pombe.

claim: The assembly dynamics of the actin cytoskeleton are functionally optimized.
source: For example, the numbers of the S. pombe homologs of Las17 and Myo3/5 also peak briefly before the peak of actin molecules (Berro et al., 2010; Sirotkin et al., 2010), suggesting that the assembly dynamics of the actin cytoskeleton are functionally optimized.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the similarity of dynamics across species.

claim: In S. pombe the Las17 homolog Wsp1 is recruited together with myosin just prior to actin polymerization.
source: However, there are also some clear differences: in S. pombe the Las17 homolog Wsp1 is recruited together with myosin just prior to actin polymerization (Berro et al., 2010; Sirotkin et al., 2010; Arasada and Pollard, 2011) whereas in S. cerevisiae Las17 localizes >10 s before myosins are recruited and actin polymerization starts (Kaksonen et al., 2003; Figure 5).

claim: In S. cerevisiae Las17 localizes >10 s before myosins are recruited and actin polymerization starts.
source: However, there are also some clear differences: in S. pombe the Las17 homolog Wsp1 is recruited together with myosin just prior to actin polymerization (Berro et al., 2010; Sirotkin et al., 2010; Arasada and Pollard, 2011) whereas in S. cerevisiae Las17 localizes >10 s before myosins are recruited and actin polymerization starts (Kaksonen et al., 2003; Figure 5).

claim: Rvs assembly and disassembly are tightly coupled to the membrane shape changes.
source: Rvs assembly and disassembly are tightly coupled to the membrane shape changes (Figure 4).

claim: Rvs molecules may get recruited by a specific membrane curvature at the invagination, but protein–protein interactions may also have a role in the recruitment.
source: Rvs molecules may get recruited by a specific membrane curvature at the invagination, but protein–protein interactions may also have a role in the recruitment (Ren et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation.

claim: Just before scission, the membrane invagination is densely covered by Rvs molecules.
source: Just before scission, the membrane invagination is densely covered by Rvs molecules.
evidence: This is supported by the reconstruction model.

claim: Scission occurs within the Rvs covered region at ~1/3 of the invagination length.
source: Scission occurs within the Rvs covered region at ∼1/3 of the invagination length (Kukulski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous CLEM data.

claim: Neither Rvs, nor the yeast homolog of dynamin Vps1, are essential for scission, but they may regulate its timing or location.
source: Neither Rvs, nor the yeast homolog of dynamin Vps1, are essential for scission, but they may regulate its timing or location (Kishimoto et al., 2011; Kukulski et al., 2012; Smaczynska-de Rooij et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The location of actin polymerization and Myo5 corresponds closely to the site of scission.
source: Interestingly, the location of actin polymerization and Myo5 corresponds closely to the site of scission, therefore polymerization and motor activities could have a role in scission (Jonsdottir and Li, 2004).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the spatial correspondence of these components.

claim: Polymerization and motor activities could have a role in scission.
source: Interestingly, the location of actin polymerization and Myo5 corresponds closely to the site of scission, therefore polymerization and motor activities could have a role in scission (Jonsdottir and Li, 2004).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation.

claim: The Rvs molecules that remain on the newly formed vesicle might have additional roles, for example, in uncoating as shown for the mammalian homolog endophilin.
source: After scission the Rvs molecules that remain on the newly formed vesicle might have additional roles, for example, in uncoating as shown for the mammalian homolog endophilin (Milosevic et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation to work on the mammalian homolog.

claim: The coat, which is initially assembled on flat membrane, starts internalizing and reorganizing when actin polymerization begins.
source: The coat, which is initially assembled on flat membrane, starts internalizing and reorganizing when actin polymerization begins.
evidence: This is an inference based on the integrated data from the study.

claim: Actin polymerization is initiated close to the plasma membrane where Las17 is located and the region of polymerization remains at the base of the invagination throughout vesicle budding.
source: Actin polymerization is initiated close to the plasma membrane where Las17 is located and the region of polymerization remains at the base of the invagination throughout vesicle budding.

claim: When the invagination has formed, actin is likely polymerizing in a circular region surrounding the invagination.
source: When the invagination has formed, actin is likely polymerizing in a circular region surrounding the invagination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the geometry of the invagination and the location of polymerization.

claim: Initially, actin polymerization might also be triggered in a circular region at the rim of the coat, where Sla1, a regulator of actin nucleation, is also located.
source: Initially, actin polymerization might also be triggered in a circular region at the rim of the coat, where Sla1, a regulator of actin nucleation, is also located.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the location of Sla1.

claim: Continued filament nucleation and polymerization at the plasma membrane would push the older filaments into the cell generating a flow of actin filaments.
source: Continued filament nucleation and polymerization at the plasma membrane would push the older filaments into the cell generating a flow of actin filaments.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mechanism of actin polymerization.

claim: The organization of the endocytic actin network bears striking similarity to the organization of actin at the leading edge of migrating animal cells where actin filaments nucleated by the Arp2/3 complex polymerize and push against the plasma membrane.
source: The organization of the endocytic actin network bears striking similarity to the organization of actin at the leading edge of migrating animal cells where actin filaments nucleated by the Arp2/3 complex polymerize and push against the plasma membrane (Pollard and Borisy, 2003).
evidence: This is an inference comparing the endocytic actin network to the leading edge of migrating cells, supported by a citation.

claim: The actin binding domains of Sla2 are ideally positioned at the surface of the endocytic coat to capture the actin filaments that are moving away from the plasma membrane.
source: The actin binding domains of Sla2 are ideally positioned at the surface of the endocytic coat to capture the actin filaments that are moving away from the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is an inference based on the orientation and position of Sla2.

claim: The actin scaffold is rigid enough to transmit the forces produced by the polymerization at the plasma membrane so that Sla2 can, together with Ent1, transmit the force from the actin polymerization to the membrane.
source: We suggest that the actin scaffold is rigid enough to transmit the forces produced by the polymerization at the plasma membrane so that Sla2 can, together with Ent1 (Skruzny et al., 2012), transmit the force from the actin polymerization to the membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative model for force transmission, supported by a citation.

claim: The coiled-coil region of Sla2 contains a clathrin-binding motif.
source: The coiled-coil region separating the terminal domains contains a clathrin-binding motif (Engqvist-Goldstein et al., 2001; Boettner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sla2 molecules could span the clathrin lattice, which is about 22 nm from the membrane surface, and interact simultaneously with the membrane, with clathrin, and with actin filaments on the cytoplasmic side of the clathrin lattice.
source: Therefore, Sla2 molecules could span the clathrin lattice, which is about 22 nm from the membrane surface (Vigers et al., 1986), and interact simultaneously with the membrane, with clathrin, and with actin filaments on the cytoplasmic side of the clathrin lattice.

claim: Sla1, End3, and Pan1 form a complex, which is implicated in the regulation of actin assembly.
source: Sla1 and End3, together with a third protein Pan1, form a complex, which is implicated in the regulation of actin assembly (Holtzman et al., 1993; Bénédetti et al., 1994; Tang et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sla1 is localized in a ring of ~50 nm in diameter, which can fit well around the tip of the endocytic membrane invagination of ~30 nm in diameter.

claim: Sla1 and End3 are late-assembling coat proteins.

source: As Sla1 and End3 are late-assembling coat proteins (Kaksonen et al., 2005; Newpher et al., 2005), they could assemble at the rim of a pre-existing early coat.

source: Interestingly, Sla2 and Pan1, have been suggested to capture short cytosolic actin filaments that could serve as 'mother filaments' to recruit the Arp2/3 complex and to initiate the assembly of the actin network (Chen and Pollard, 2013).

claim: The endocytic coat exhibits a highly organized and dynamic molecular architecture during vesicle budding.
source: Taken together, our data demonstrate that the endocytic coat exhibits a highly organized and dynamic molecular architecture during vesicle budding.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all the data presented in the study.

claim: At high concentration BAR domain proteins can actively induce membrane curvature.
source: BAR domain proteins can sense membrane curvature and they can actively induce membrane curvature at high concentration (Peter et al., 2004; Mizuno et al., 2010; Mim et al., 2012).

source: This Rvs lattice could therefore support the membrane tubule and prevent premature fission (Kukulski et al., 2012).

source: Therefore, the center of mass of Rvs molecules would rapidly shift due to localized disassembly without actual movement of the Rvs lattice.
